slides.title: Tell It Another Way
bullets: Prepare to read, discuss and write
slides.narration: Welcome to Grade 5 English, Unit 7: Tell It Another Way. Unit 7 explores point of view: who tells a story, and how that choice changes what a reader sees. You will compare two first-person accounts of one market morning, then follow a Year 5 class in Ayensu who uncover a hidden mural and argue about what it means. Along the way you will learn to separate facts from opinions, to use phrases such as I think that and In my opinion, and to agree or disagree politely with a reason. The unit ends with you retelling a familiar story through a brand-new narrator's eyes. In this short lecture, preview the key ideas and prepare for the independent lesson.

slides.title: What you will achieve
bullets: Explain what point of view means and identify the narrator in a text.
Compare two versions of the same event told from different perspectives and explain what changes.
Describe how changing the narrator changes the mood, detail, and feeling of a story.
slides.narration: By the end of this unit, you will be able to explain what point of view means and identify the narrator in a text. You will also compare two versions of the same event told from different perspectives and explain what changes. You will also describe how changing the narrator changes the mood, detail, and feeling of a story. Keep these goals in mind as you work.

slides.title: Language for precise thinking
slides.narration: Your vocabulary work begins with these words: local, urban, rural, spacious, continent, colonial. Listen to each pronunciation in the vocabulary lab, study its meaning in context, and use the word accurately in your own discussion and writing.

slides.title: Read critically
bullets: Two Voices from the Market: Omar's Account
Two Voices from the Market: Amal's Account
slides.narration: The reading sequence includes Two Voices from the Market: Omar's Account and Two Voices from the Market: Amal's Account. Read actively. Identify each text's central ideas, notice viewpoint and reliability, and support every inference with relevant evidence from the text.

slides.title: Facts and Opinions: Telling Them Apart
bullets: A fact can be checked and proved with evidence. An opinion tells us what one person thinks or feels, so somebody else may reasonably disagree with it.
slides.narration: The first language focus is Facts and Opinions: Telling Them Apart. A fact can be checked and proved with evidence. An opinion tells us what one person thinks or feels, so somebody else may reasonably disagree with it. Notice the structure in the model examples, then apply it deliberately in connected sentences and paragraphs.

slides.title: Use English for a real purpose
bullets: Writing 1: Retell a Story from a New Point of View
Explain, support and improve your ideas
slides.narration: In speaking, you will complete Speaking 1: Hot-Seating a Narrator. Organise your ideas, use evidence and respond clearly to questions. In writing, you will plan, draft, check and revise. Use the success criteria before submitting your work.

slides.title: You are ready to begin
bullets: Activities, quiz and optional live sessions
slides.narration: You are ready to begin. Start with the vocabulary lab, continue through reading and comprehension, apply the grammar focus, and complete the speaking and writing practices. Use the AI tutor for hints and feedback any time, and bring your questions to a live session too if you join one.
